1.title: Know what a financial consultant does
1.intro: A financial consultant helps people or small firms understand money and make better choices. Learn the basics first.
pts: Define income, expense, asset, debt and net worth.
Describe the difference between advice, education and selling a product.
Explain who a consultant can serve: households, small firms, community groups.
List words: budget, cash flow, interest, risk, return.
1.ex: A café owner earns 9,000 a month and spends 8,400. Income minus expense is 600. The consultant first shows this in one simple table.
1.act: Write your own one-month income and expense list and mark what is fixed and what changes.
1.std: Task: define core money terms. Condition: using your own month. Standard: five terms used correctly in a one-page table.

2.title: Read basic money records
2.intro: You cannot advise without reading numbers. Start with the three basic reports.
pts: Describe the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow list in simple words.
Apply ratios: profit margin, debt to assets, days of cash.
Check that records match bank statements.
Explain why cash and profit are not the same.
2.ex: A shop shows profit on paper but unpaid customer bills. Cash is low, so it struggles to pay rent. The consultant shows the gap in a cash list.
2.act: Read one sample set of small-firm records and write five plain-word findings.
2.std: Task: read basic records. Condition: a sample set. Standard: ratios correct and five findings written in plain words.

3.title: Follow the rules in Canada
3.intro: Giving money advice is regulated. What you may say or sell depends on your licence and province. Check with the regulator.
pts: Explain that advising on investments, insurance or loans often needs a provincial licence; check the securities or insurance regulator.
Describe the difference between a title like adviser and a protected title; check the current rule.
Apply the duty to know your client and to avoid conflicts of interest.
Check anti-money-laundering and privacy rules that apply to your work.
3.ex: Rules table row: Investment advice | provincial securities regulator | registration needed before advising | before first paid advice | registration proof kept.
3.act: Make a rules table for your province: what you can do unlicensed, and what needs a licence.
3.std: Task: map the rules. Condition: official regulator pages. Standard: each row has an enforcer, an action and a checked date.

4.title: Build a client plan
4.intro: A plan starts with the client's goals and facts, not with products.
pts: Build a client fact sheet: goals, income, costs, debts, savings, time frame.
Apply a simple budget: needs, wants, savings; adjust to the client.
Compare options for a goal such as an emergency fund or debt payoff.
Write advice in plain words with the reason for each step.
4.ex: Client has 6,000 in card debt at a high rate and no savings. Plan: small emergency fund first, then extra payments on the highest-rate debt. Reasons are written.
4.act: Build a plan for a practice client using a fact sheet and a one-page action list.
4.std: Task: build a plan. Condition: practice client. Standard: goals, facts, options and reasons all written in plain words.

5.title: Work with risk and numbers
5.intro: Every choice has risk. Show it clearly and test the bad case.
pts: Explain interest, compound growth and inflation in plain words.
Compute loan payments and savings growth with a free calculator.
Evaluate risk: loss, delay, fraud, change in rates; give a bad-case number.
Check claims such as very high safe returns; treat them as warnings.
5.ex: Saving 200 a month for 5 years at a low steady rate gives about 12,000 plus a little interest. A promise of doubling in a year is a warning sign.
5.act: Test one savings goal and one loan at two interest rates and write what changes.
5.std: Task: test a money choice. Condition: two rate cases. Standard: figures correct and the bad case explained.

6.title: Find clients and set your fee
6.intro: Clients pay for clear results and trust. Be open about how you are paid.
pts: Build a one-page offer: who, problem, result, process, fee.
Compare fee types: hourly, fixed, monthly; state them before work starts.
Write an engagement letter with scope, fee, privacy and what you do not do.
Track the funnel: contacts, calls, proposals, signed clients.
6.ex: Fixed fee for a cash-flow review: 4 hours work, 2 hours meeting. At 150 an hour that is 900. Teaching figure only; check local prices.
6.act: Write an offer and engagement letter and book five discovery calls.
6.std: Task: win a first client. Condition: four weeks. Standard: offer under one page and a signed letter with scope and fee.

7.title: Protect client money and data
7.intro: Trust is your main asset. Never mix client money with yours.
pts: Apply the rule: keep client records private and locked, with strong sign-in.
Check scams: fake invoices, urgent transfers, identity theft; teach clients to spot them.
Explain why you never take client money into your own account unless the law and licence allow it.
Create a record of advice given, with dates and reasons.
7.ex: A client gets an urgent email from a fake supplier. The consultant has a call-back rule: confirm any new bank details by phone with a known number.
7.act: Write a privacy note, a call-back rule and a risk register of eight rows.
7.std: Task: protect a client. Condition: practice case. Standard: each risk has a control, an owner and a review date.

8.title: Run your practice for real
8.intro: Now serve real clients within your licence and keep learning.
pts: Run a 90-day pilot with two or three clients, or a community workshop.
Review each case: plan, result, client feedback, mistakes.
Create a 12-month plan with licensing, learning and fee goals.
Lead others: train a helper to prepare fact sheets and follow the checklist.
8.ex: Stop rule: if the practice costs more than it earns after 90 days, change the offer. Result and decision are recorded with numbers.
8.act: Run the pilot, write the review and present your plan to a panel of three.
8.std: Task: run a consulting pilot. Condition: 90 days, within licence limits. Standard: results compared with the stop rule and rules re-checked with the regulator.

quiz: What is net worth?
Assets minus debts.
Why are cash and profit different?
Profit includes unpaid bills; cash is money actually in hand.
Who regulates investment advice in Canada?
Provincial securities regulators; check yours.
What goes in a client fact sheet?
Goals, income, costs, debts, savings and time frame.
Why test the bad case?
To see if the plan still works when things go wrong.
How can you spot a likely scam?
Promises of very high safe returns or urgent transfer requests.
What must an engagement letter include?
Scope, fee, privacy and what is not included.
What is a call-back rule?
Confirm any new bank details by phone using a known number.
Why not mix client money with yours?
It risks loss, breaks trust and may break the law.
What if you are unsure whether you need a licence?
Ask the regulator and keep the answer in writing.
